clues: This city stands on the Waal River in the east of the Netherlands. It lies close to the border with Germany.
This is one of the warmest cities in its land in summer. No tall ranges run north to south here, so the weather can shift all at once.
This city was the first in its land to be known as a city in Roman times. In 2005, folk here marked two thousand years of town life.
Each year this city hosts a famed march that lasts four long days. The march is the town's best known event of the whole year.
This town has been a home of Radboud University since 1923. That school first opened its doors as a Catholic school.
